main_body: A palm tree: a slender curved trunk with a drooping frond canopy of green leaves at the top
top_band: none as a distinct band; the canopy is a leafy crown of greens (rows ~1-16) with light green centre, no separate top surface over a front face
evidence: Organic palm tree. Canopy is a fan of fronds seen from the side/slightly above, and the trunk is a thin curved column. It is organic, so the strict horizontal top/front structure does not apply. There is a crown with highlight on top and fronds drooping, which reads acceptably as a plant in 3/4 style. Nothing marks a flat elevation or plan. Organic objects are not judged by the plank-top contract, so this passes.

style.evidence: The references are big leafy broadleaf trees with many clumped leaf greens, dark-green material outlines and detailed bark and roots. The candidate palm has about 4 greens in the fronds and 3-4 tan tones on the trunk. Its outline is a uniform near-black line around the fronds and trunk, giving a sticker look, whereas the references separate forms by dark green tones. Trunk has banded ring texture but is fairly regular, and the fronds are smooth bands with little leaf-clump variation. Per-tile colour counts are lower than the references.
